utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So there are numerous problems.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We're at 93% login rates.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The app is working.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Will there be an operator error or an issue with a device?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: But that's what our training program is meant to do.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I would like to see our drivers in attendance performing at 100% in terms of logging in.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So there's 100% visibility.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: But we're over 90%, and you probably do have an example or two of a driver not being able to log on.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And those are things we solution in real time.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We have a help desk for that.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: But I would say they're motivated to show progress, and we do have liquidated damages, to go back to Speaker Menon's point.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: In the pilot of the logins, we chose not to issue liquidated damages at that point in time because we were still in a pilot stage of learning from, was the device communicating?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Was the console working?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Was the unit itself working?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Does the driver, an attendant, new to the system, is there a technical issue?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So when you're doing a pilot, we chose effectively not to implement liquidated damage, but we are now.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So to follow up the other question.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: You mentioned a help desk for...

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: drivers, but parents also have concerns.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And parents will say they call the Office of People Transportation, they get bounced to the DOE, they bounce them back to you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: When will families be able to log complaints directly in that app?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We have that identified as an enhancement.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So as soon as...

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: You have to pay for that too?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We will be working on that as an enhancement.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We, to your point about the routing suite, we will start this September with all Curb to School.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We'll have the routing optimization.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: They will be essentially complete with the project.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: What routing software do you use now?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So we use a combination of FoxPro and Edulog.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And just as it relates to the expenditure was mentioned, $50 million to modernize our fleet.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Concurrent with that same window, we spent nearly $15 billion in services.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And VIA does much more than just GPS location tracking.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so there's a lot of development that went into the system that is not seen by parent or seen by public per se.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: But happy to have an offline meeting about what does the overall STRIDE program look like in our modernization and what did VIA look like concurrent with that.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Yeah, the issue with VIA isn't just $36 or $51.7 million.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It's that we've paid them for this contract, and the routes are not optimized.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And you're using EduLog, which is from what year?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: You have the year.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: It's a couple decades old.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: You can turn the mic on.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: It's on.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: It's old.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: It's a couple of decades old.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: How old?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: I could get you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: Is it 1994?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: I'll get you a date.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It was in the 1900s.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Do you guys remember MS-DOS?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Commodore 64?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Ah, that's, you know why you remember that?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Because you're all old like me.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Like the software.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And Fox Pro as well?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Same thing in the 90s?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: Similarly.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Similar, okay.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And we've paid via, and this is the frustration, that we've paid for a service, like route optimization, and we're gonna get to some of the routes in a second, or in a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I wanna let a few colleagues ask some questions first, and then we'll get to some of the actual routes, what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: But we've paid money for a service that has not been provided.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And the impact of that is students being late to school or picked up early from school or spending more than an appropriate amount of time on the bus.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And it is heartbreaking to hear when a parent tells you that their child soils himself on a regular basis because they spend so long on the bus.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And we're going to look at some of the roots later.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: To talk about why that may be the case.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Does the DOE own the software that VIA is building for the DOE?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So a little bit of breakdown of what we're working on.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The hardware, the GPS, and connectivity, these are types of things we have to pay for.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And that's, when you look at the cost breakdown, there's $10 million in terms of we have to buy the units, we have to buy the installation.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: There are things that are costly when you times them by 10,000.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So it's not necessarily, these are like isolated expenditures.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The software platform is $5 million, but it is not proprietary towards the New York City public school system.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: This is essentially testing it on the New York City market.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: They're going to go sell it to some other market.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Well, this is the service that the local law compelled them to provide.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And that's hardware in addition to the GPS tab that goes on each and every bus?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So it's a great point.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The redundancy of the GeoTab provides us another layer of safe operation.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We like to know how a bus is physically performing.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: This is not a route.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: These are not the same.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: These are mutually exclusive.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: When you think about the GeoTab can tell John and I on a really cold night how many batteries are dying and where we need to jumpstart a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: It'll tell us who needs an oil change.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: It'll tell us what driver sharp cornering or harsh braking or rapid acceleration.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The GeoTab telematics is more about the behavior of the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: the condition and functioning of the engine than it is about GPS.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: While it does provide GPS location information, it is, for us, a safety tool.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And I want to thank DCAS for the partnership.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: But I understand that these systems don't talk to each other, that there are certain companies or interested parties who want the API key so they can query that data as well.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The system of GeoTab is not meant to be student-facing.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: These are totally separate systems.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The GeoTab is part of our, actually one of the things we're most proud of, is the Vision Zero driver training program.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Each school bus driver has an evaluation.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And the vehicle is on the school console and our console, and so we could look at who is rapid acceleration, who is harsh braking.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: This is about a vehicle diagnostic and behavior, not about a student route.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so while there was, I think, an interest in saying, could we use the technology together,

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: It is not what our goal is.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Our goal is to keep that to be this is the vehicle behavior because at any given moment, we could take a vehicle out of service, and that geotab is part of the wiring harness.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So that will not reflect a route that switches if a bus is being, you know, the tires changed or an oil change or brakes being replaced.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So we keep these things separate for a purpose, but it does provide redundancy on location.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I'm going to get back to the roots later, but I do want to call in a few colleagues for council member questions.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Starting with Councilmember Salvina Brooks-Powers.

chapters.summary: Lee asks about VIA app accuracy and language access; DOE says app usage has grown and translation is being improved, but acknowledges gaps.
chapters.title: Council Member Lee questions DOE on VIA app accuracy and language access

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: We're passing notes in class.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: How appropriate.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: I promise they're my remarks, not the chair's.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Dinnowitz, for convening today's important hearing.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: And thank you to everyone here to testify.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: I want to take a moment to address a deeply troubling incident that recently came to light involving six nonverbal special education students who were left traveling on a school bus for more than four hours without their parents or school

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: being notified about their whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: As an aunt to a nonverbal nephew, I find this incident particularly disturbing.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Every day, families across our city place enormous trust in the individuals responsible for transporting their children to and from school.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: They do so with the expectation that their children will be safe and treated with the care and dignity they deserve.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: What happened to these six children represents an unacceptable breakdown in that responsibility.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: These are kids who may not be able to communicate when something is wrong or advocate for themselves.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: That makes it even more critical that we have strong safeguards and meaningful accountability at every level of our school transportation system.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: While I understand that the driver and bus matron involved have been removed from student transportation duties, that alone isn't enough.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: We need answers about how this happened and what concrete steps are being taken to ensure

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: sure no other child or family experiences something like this again.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: In recent weeks, I've had several discussions with Queensborough President Donovan Richards, who is also a parent of a school-aged child, and we both are keenly focused on ensuring that transportation for our students is

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: as safe as possible, which is why I strongly support Councilmember Ressler's bill, Intro 835, which would help provide a roadmap of ways we can improve school bus performance across the city.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: So I'm really happy to hear that the administration is in support of this legislation.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: With that, I have a few questions, and I'll ask the three.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: I can repeat whatever you want afterwards.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: So first.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: How could a school bus carrying six students remain unaccounted for for more than four hours without triggering an alert to the school, DOE, or the student's family?

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: What protocols were in place at the time, and where specifically did they break down?

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Two, what systems does DOE currently have in place to monitor school bus locations and ensure that students, particularly those with disabilities and complex communication needs, arrive safely and on time?

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Are there automatic alerts or intervention procedures when a bus is significantly delayed or deviates from its assigned route?

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: And lastly, beyond the disciplinary actions taken against the individuals involved, what specific corrective measures has DOE implemented?

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: since this incident.

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Are additional safeguards or legislative changes needed from your perspective to prevent this from happening again?

utterances.speaker: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Thank you for the question.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And that matter was wholly unacceptable to all the families impacted.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We offer our apologies.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: That is not the expectation ultimately of the system.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We want to make sure that students are directed to school quickly and on time.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So as it relates to when we were made aware that the driver and attendant were not getting to school, we reported that to the special commissioner of investigations

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: and ultimately suspended them immediately and then ultimately terminated both individuals.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The process where it broke down is that they didn't call the dispatch, number one.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: They didn't notify OPT.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: In a moment's notice, especially in the city of New York, you could stop virtually anywhere and ask for directions.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so the behavior there was completely unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So one of the things in terms of protocols, those were the reasons for the termination.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: But what could we do better going forward?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So in real time, we're developing alongside of council members, wrestlers intro bill is to make sure we're tracking time from distance from home to school and ultimately completing a route.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So I think what you're looking for and what we're looking at is geofencing and putting a time bind on every route.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So we're

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: If it's not completed, we would get that triggered alert.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So absent that, we would just rely on the company to report a delay or a school delay.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Going forward, we're looking to have that automated with a timing alert.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Like this is when a route begins.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: This is when it ends.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: This is when it begins late.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And we can, like schools, there is real-time tracking.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: At the school level with the school-based console, at the company level they have it, and at OPT.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So we have the ability in our emergency operations center, we can look at all buses in real time at any given time.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So I think to your point, we have to develop alongside with Council Member Ressler's report about here's the time of the route, here's when we have to actually signal an alert, like why is it so late?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So we'll come back to that.

chapters.summary: A foster parent testifies that a child's bus route was canceled without notice, forcing them to arrange alternative transportation and miss work.
chapters.title: Public witness describes bus route cancellation for foster child

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Council Member Ressler?

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chair Dinowitz.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Once again, really appreciate your leadership on this.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I will just say, Deputy Chancellor, you are a treasure, and we appreciate you and are grateful for your years of service and problem solving.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I'm still going to give you guys a hard time.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So yesterday was a pretty average day in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Nice weather, nothing major going on, no gridlock alert days or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: 211 buses were delayed, 434 kids on board.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Over half of those were delayed for well over 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I understand it's a large system and there will always be some delays.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: It's a big city.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: There's lots of challenges.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: But what's your target for daily on time percentage of buses?

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Is 211 delayed buses an acceptable day?

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I think that's half as much as the average last year.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So maybe that is a good day.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Could you give some context on kind of what's our daily goal?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So with thinking about transportation every day, the goal is 100% on time arrival.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And we're looking at systems development that will help us do this better with predictive analytics around when we have to start route sequence first, when we have to end the route sequence.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And I think...

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Observing lunch programs, I mean breakfast programs, we want to make sure we're getting in on time and working with the school on the right session time.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We also want to, I spend a lot of time speaking with Deputy

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Chancellor Foti, and we're in lockstep about this notion of, you know, whether we bring student to service or we bring service to student.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so the goal in most of what we're doing now is figuring out how to make sure we bring the service to the student and reduce lengthy commutes, increase our time.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We see through the data.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And I'm sure this is intuitive, but like the shorter the route, the less the delay.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So we look at our five mile or less routes.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: They're not the routes that are running late.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: It's the 10, the 15, the 20.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And it's the oftentimes where we have mandates for limited time travel.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so the route can get longer.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And that's where I think we see delays.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I think we see delays.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: On the number of individuals on a bus route too, if there's 12 students versus eight students, and so the time to board buses.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The idea here is to get to no late buses.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so I think with your tool and others, we're gonna be able to shine a light better on who's performing, because there are outliers in every scenario, and who's not, and I think it'll help us with our vendor report card and holding those accountable that can't get kids to school on time, but the goal is,

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: every bus on time every day.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I appreciate that and it is helpful.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I know that my colleagues have dug in on this a little and I want to continue around VIA.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: My understanding is that their system requires drivers to log into the app every single day in order to track the bus location.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Why would DOE kind of choose a system that requires this opt-in?

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I know that you just noted a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: go to Chair Dynowitz's questions that GeoTab was not intended to be student-facing or family-facing, but GeoTabs are installed on buses, can track locations at all times without requiring someone to turn them on.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: It's a much better model because then we would actually know where every bus is at all times.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Could you elaborate a little further, and are you moving away from an opt-in system with VIA?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So I very much appreciate the question.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The idea is that we match route and driver.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So the login is a lot about security.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: It's a lot about the individual.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so for the first time ever, we have a new driver and attendant system, and we have a lens system that connects the DMV.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And we know in real time, at any given time, who can log in and who can't.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And I think with the provisions and the safety clearances we put in place in the system that

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: via built for us required login.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So I knew who the exact driver was driving the exact vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And that's important to us.

chapters.summary: Narcisse asks why DOE assessed only $1.7 million of $44.3 million in potential penalties; DOE says it is reviewing penalty collection and contractor scorecards.
chapters.title: Council Member Narcisse questions DOE on penalties and contractor accountability

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I think the GeoTab allows for uncertainty around doubling of routes or drivers sharing.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And we built this for security purposes.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: But I just, I apologize for interrupting, but those feel like two separate things.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: It's perfectly reasonable for you to want to be able to ensure that the person who's driving the bus is the person who it's supposed to be and that they've logged in for verification, for safety of all.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: That's different from us just having the automated data available to all of us on where the bus is, whether it's on time, how it's moving.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And by forcing that login, which is not happening too often, we're not getting that data in a publicly accessible, easily trackable way.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Yeah, I look forward to sharing our login data on a more regular basis.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I think it's something we could produce for the public, but at 93%, I want to be at 100%.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I think it gives us the full suite and the full transparency of what we built for families.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And while not every family is logging in to see where it is, I want to make sure every driver has logged in to make sure it's available.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Do you mind if I continue for a moment?

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: How many penalties does DOE, so you say 93% of the time is login.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: To be clear, I think that's totally unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: We need this information comprehensively, and I frankly think

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: The opt-in model is just poor program design.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: But that being said, how many penalties has DOE assessed to companies for failing to turn on the VIA app?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Yeah, so any instance where they're not logging in, they are issued liquidated damages.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So I don't know, John, if you brought the data with you.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: I have the overall damages that we've done for all violations.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: I could get the via violations quickly if I could just circle back in a few moments.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I mean, I just, you know, my understanding is failure to turn on the GPS functionality can result in a $75 per violation.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And that the city has left tens of millions of dollars on the table in failing to actually issue those violations on school bus companies that might change their behavior, why would we not be issuing those violations every single time?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: That instance, we do do it.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: That was during the pilot period when we were negotiating the contract extension where we said there was more training, tech training, tech support needed.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So the liquidated damages then were suspended as an act of choice of the administration.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Now you're charging fine every single time that the GPS is not being turned on.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Yes, and I get reports on it, and we do actually follow through.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: If you could provide that data or look for that data while other folks jump in, because Jared Genowitz is giving me a dirty look.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Just smiles.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I do want to point out that the app also requires...

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Parents to log in every time it's accessed.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: That's something that I don't do.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: with any of my apps, or most of them, I would note you can only see the arrival for that day within an hour or so.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: No history of latenesses.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So a parent is not empowered to have that data in front of them.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Will you update the app to ensure that a lateness log or history is available to families?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Well, I want this tool to be as useful for families as possible, so we'll connect on this and take that back to our programs to see what is visible.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: If there's a time band or look back, we can talk to the developers on that.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to take that as a yes.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: You'll put the information that's available to them within that hour.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: You'll keep on the app.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Let me confirm.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I want to talk to her.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I want to make sure exactly what you're asking is what we can provide.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Okay, and one other note about that is that the bus service does not connect well with schools on half days.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: This is something I mentioned before, but it also, when the bus drivers, as well on the apps, they are told they're doing something wrong by logging in on those half days, if a kid has a half day.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So you definitely need to look into that.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I'm now going to call on Council Member Joseph.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Denowitz.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: When I chaired this committee, we held hearings on school buses in 2022, 2024, and 2025.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Each time New York City Public School came, they made commitments on GPS, apps for parents, new routing technology, better communications with family.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: So today I want to go through some of those commitments that were made here on the record and see where you are.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: In 2024, OPT told me that its goal was 150,000 parents to download the login to the app.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: How many families are actively using it?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And right now, families can see their child getting on and off the bus in a nicer bus route pilot, which covers about 818 of the 9,000 routes.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: When will every family have this?

chapters.summary: An advocate testifies that the current oversight system fails students with disabilities and calls for enforceable contracts, real penalties, and public data.
chapters.title: Public witness from advocacy group calls for stronger oversight

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Can you give us a timeline?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So our goal remains every parent does download the app.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The local law requires that we offer this service to families.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so we're working with families to let them know that it's available.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The goal remains we want every family to take advantage of it.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: John, I don't know if you have the daily logins.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: If I had a room full of parents here, would their hands go up in agreement with you?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: I can't speak for other parents.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: What I can say is in 2024, the average daily usage was around 1,800 per day.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: It is currently over 10,000, and it continues to rise.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: How many parents do you carry every day in the school bus system?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: How many parents did you say use this app?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: The math is not mapping.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: So that means not every parent in New York City who has a child in the system is using this app.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: I think there should be better outreach in reaching families and getting them to download this in languages they can also understand.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: Fully aligned with you there.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: We will boost our communications.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: I think the app is successful.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: I'm a school bus parent.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: 10,000 parents and 150,000 students.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: I would love everyone's support to get the word out about the app.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: I know it works.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: It's successful.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: It's a value add for families.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: I would encourage anyone.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: who's a school bus parent, to download the app, get the Nixa credentials, log in, and test it out.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Your family engagement unit needs to work with parents to get them on board.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Yeah, we'll absolutely, that's great feedback.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We'll work with our family engagement team to see why families haven't downloaded it and if we can encourage more to do so.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Yeah, that would be great.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And the right time.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: In 2024, OPT told this committee it tries to keep rides between boroughs to two hours.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: At the hearing, I described a Brooklyn student who would get on the bus from 6 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: It wouldn't get to school until 8.20.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: That's two hours and 20 minutes late.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And miss all of their relative services.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And got to school in Manhattan at 820.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: New York City Public School took the control of that, that a goal was 75 to 90 minutes within a borough and 105 to 20 minutes between boroughs.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Did the two-hour ceiling become the target?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And are families being told this?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: No, we're doing work every day to reduce distance.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I've seen stories even in the paper and the news about long travel, and we see that on paper, but I think the goal ultimately is to continually reduce distance traveled.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: It's ultimately correlated to time, but when we have long distances,

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: You know, we have routes of 25 miles, 30 miles, 35 miles, 40 miles.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: How many students do we have that's riding the bus about 90 minutes or longer?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Do we have the data today?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We can pull that data for you.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Medical staff on buses.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: In 2022, OPT said it was working to hire nurses for routes serving students with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Vendors report now that shows medical route staffers dropped from 33 to 3.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: What happened to that hiring effort?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: How many students whose IEP require a medical profession on the bus or without bus services because of this?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So, John, I don't know if I take this one.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: As of this week, there are around 325 students that have an IEP nurse recommendation on their IEP.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: That's 325.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: We are working to assign a mandated nurse for roughly 17 students and are working with urgency in order to get those services arranged.

chapters.summary: Schulman asks about broken air conditioning and safety incidents; DOE describes inspection protocols and incident reporting, but acknowledges more work is needed.
chapters.title: Council Member Schulman questions DOE on bus air conditioning and safety

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: So how many students we have at home currently?

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: There are 325 that have the recommendation for a nurse, and we are working to arrange that coverage for 17 students.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: 17 students.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And language access.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: In 2024, OPT told me that the app will be in whatever language the parent's phone is set up.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: But many families, including Haitian Creole speakers in my district, may have phones that are not set up in their language.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Which language or bus alerts and the apps and the OPT hotlines is available today?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: The app is available in all required languages, and the families can set their phone to their preferred language, and the app will appear in that language.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: That has not changed.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: That has not changed.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Last school year, how many OPT calls for complaints came in languages other than English?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: You will get that back to the committee?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And OPT's own capacity, staffing in OPT, you have vacancies.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: How many vacancies do you have, and what's the timeline to fill them?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: We're at 150 headcount at current, 10 vacancies posted.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And when is the timeline to fill those vacancies?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: As soon as we can.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: They're posted, so as fast as we can conduct the interview process.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And you'll report that.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Chair, I'll come back for the second round because I want to talk about foster youth and students in temporary housing.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Joseph.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Councilmember Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I first want to thank you.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Because the Moran team is very helpful constantly.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I call often about buses, and you're always responsive, and I want to thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: One other question.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: In your testimony, you did indicate how many more routes and students and so on.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I assume, but I'd love to know because you didn't say why.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Obviously, people move around, but I think it has to do with more kids with IEPs and more kids going, I'm afraid, to schools other than public because the need is there and the IEP fits a different school.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I just want to get a sense of it.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Big number.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: What do you think it is?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Yeah, I think we're very much excited about the work with Dial and Deputy Chancellor Foti's team about increased opportunities closer to home and increased offerings across our portfolio.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So I think a lot of it is about new program openings.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so, John, if you want to take about the expansion of the programs.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It seems to me there are a lot of kids going, I'm getting the calls from somebody living in Queens going to school in Manhattan because they have an IEP and that school is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I'd love to see the student and the student would like to stay in Queens with the appropriate school.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: Well, we would love to connect with you about that student's particular circumstances.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I got a whole bunch of them.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: You're taking care of them already.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I call constantly.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: You know, our goal here is to provide high-quality programs within every community so that students do not need to travel long distances.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: We are, you know, there's been a lot in the news around declining enrollment, special education enrollment in New York City public schools

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: is increasing, up from 183,000 a few years ago up to over 190,000 students, school-age students with IEPs within our public schools.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: And so while we're seeing increases in District 75, I'm also proud to report that we're seeing more students receive services through our high-quality autism programs, NEST, Horizon, AIMS, for example, within their local communities.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: I appreciate all of former Chair Joseph's advocacy during her time as the Ed Committee Chair.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: She talked about the hearings that we had in the past.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: And so, you know, during school year 23, 24, for example, we had 3,800 seats for students in autism programs in local public schools.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: Since that time, we've increased 52% in seats that are available in local communities, nearly 2,000 seats more than we had back then.

chapters.summary: A parent testifies that their child with autism was left on a bus after the route ended, and calls for mandatory incident reporting and verified handoffs.
chapters.title: Public witness describes child with autism left on bus

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: And that's through the advocacy of this council.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: Now 5,800 seats for students in Nest, Horizon, and Ames within our public school.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: Seeing investments from this administration as well, really excited about building our first ever preschool special education programs, which we launched this fall, which we're very excited about.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: And this administration is committed to deepening the work.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: We opened up an additional 31 new autism programs this fall, including 23 AIMS programs, six NEST programs, and two Horizon programs.

utterances.speaker: John Hammer
utterances.text: Deputy Chancellor Moran said we got to get kids in the local communities as a real lever for change.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Next question.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: People are confused.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Do I call OPS or do I call the bus company?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Has that been settled?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Because that comes up a lot.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: When there's a problem.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Excellent question, and thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: It's one of the issues we're looking at currently about a unified call center.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Parents shouldn't have to decide whether they should call the bus company one day.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: or call the OPT call center.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: They call both.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I mean, certainly we know that if they call OPT, we get a number and we're tracking it.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: But I think companies vary across the 52 experiences, and so families experience it differently.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So I think one of the things we're looking to move towards is a unified call center so we have a unified experience.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I mean, as long as this call center actually answers the phone and doesn't put them on hold.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay, I'm just saying, if I was to pick one thing to do, I would say that, because that is what the parent is concerned about, and that's their first place to go, and they don't know where to go.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: A lot of people say that.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I've been clear.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I'm a nice bus fan.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So my question is, what have we learned from them, if anything?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: The rebidding of the contracts is coming up.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: What can we learn from NYC bus?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So thank you for sharing your experience.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I share a similar experience.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I think one of the things that NiceBus gives us is insight and experience we never had before.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I'm very fortunate to walk alongside Matt Berlin, the CEO of NiceBus, and learn about his forward trajectory around customer service.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Driver training, which I think is one of the most enlightening experiences for me about how we start on a CDL pipeline program and how we bring driver safety training programs within his organization.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I think it's exciting to see the work he's doing.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: doing with his data analytics and his mapping as it relates to both the geotab diagnostics and route information from VIA, but also about electrification efforts and what is ultimately needed to build the infrastructure,

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: compete for competitive grants, get grant awards, and get

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: service technicians in the electric bus industry on site to teach and to guide.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so what I would say, as one of the individuals, I was thankful to be a part of creating it.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: It was created to make an innovative space so that we could learn alongside.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I think it's done that.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so we're excited about any overages as well, where we can't find

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: a route driver connection we call and say these overages need to be picked up and so i think the driver recruitment and retention program is a big one for us as well so have you been giving them more routes along the lines that you just suggested are you yes giving them expanding their

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: their yeah they picked up over a hundred of the excess and they're well above

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: where they were last year.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay, one stupid question.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I should know this.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: His book, he got $100,000, I guess, from the feds to do electrification.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Are all your buses electric?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Are some electric?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Did you get federal money?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: That's my question.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So on electric buses, I will say we're very excited about the opportunities through the Biden infrastructure grants.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We were awarded in excess of 500.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: It was 533.

chapters.summary: Wong asks about route optimization and the VIA contract; DOE says new routing technology is being phased in and acknowledges missed deadlines.
chapters.title: Council Member Wong questions DOE on route optimization and technology

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We didn't get them as of yet.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: They're in the pipeline.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Currently, we have 114 on the road at current.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: 114 electric.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Yeah, we have 114 on the road.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We're working on infrastructure development with the ones we have and learning a lot.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: But we do have 533 coming soon.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I do want to share one thing.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Councilmember Brewer was talking about reporting.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Who do you report to?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: There's a lot of questions about who you report to.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Office of People and Transportation, DOE, 311, right?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: That you're all kind of...

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Not talking to each other, who's the point person.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I do also want to highlight that we've received complaints that your systems don't talk to each other.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So for example, a parent who updates their address and data in Nixa, that doesn't migrate over to you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And then an ATS, if it's updated then an ATS, you only receive one phone number because that's a system from like,

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I don't know, typewriter age, where people only had one phone number.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: ATS only probably has a single phone number for the bus companies, and there's not a lot of talking between systems.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Can you talk a little bit about that?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So we did sunset in terms of transportation, our reliance on ATS.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So everything is an oasis now, and if a family updates...

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: When you say you, I'm sorry to interrupt, all the companies as well, that means you get them the information?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Yeah, the source system is at the school.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So when the school meets family and information is provided, that's an oasis.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Or Nixa, that's the information we receive.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So you're saying as of...

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Today, if a family updates their information in Nix, so they've updated, that will automatically migrate to OASIS, and that will automatically migrate then to you?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Okay, that is a good update.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I want to recognize we've been joined by Councilmember Krishnan.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It's my job.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And ask Councilmember Wong for his questions.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Only five minutes, so please, short answers, please.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: It is my understanding that bus contractors get a route, get routes before the school starts.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: So when exactly do the bus contractor get the routes?

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: July, August, June, the day before, you know, when?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So we host a vendor, we call it a pick, that's in the middle of August.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So they get to select their route many times three to four weeks before.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The school year starts.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay, and what if there are changes to the route or there are additions and how does that work and then when do they get informed and when do they have to start implementing these changes?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Route adjustments happen on a nightly basis based upon student preference or student mandates through IEPs.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: There was a question previously on headcount, and then I believe...

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: The answer was the current headcount is 150.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: With 10 vacancies.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: What about pre-COVID?

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Can you give me the headcount at OPT before COVID and then how many people work there today?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I'll get that to you, but what I would say is we're focused on modernization and using our data and analytics to make sure we have everything we need.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I would say OPT is fully staffed, and we're thankful that we have the team in place, these experts that are in place at OPT.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I don't think it's a matter of resource on our side, so I would say that we found efficiencies in some of our call center operations.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We found efficiencies across our routing teams, so I'm not looking to comparable headcount to COVID.

chapters.summary: A Queens parent testifies that repeated driver callouts have left students waiting for hours and that communication from bus companies is poor.
chapters.title: Public witness describes bus driver shortage in Queens

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: But would you say that pre-COVID there are a lot more people working at OPT?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I wouldn't say a lot more, but I believe the headcount was hovering around 200.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: It was probably somewhere between 150 and 200, like many other city agencies.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: We've been subject to budget cuts and staffing reductions.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: So right now we're at about 150 with that 10 vacancy being processed now.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: It is my understanding the last time the bus companies had to submit bids, that was 2012 or 2013.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: When we rebid a portion of the contracts, correct, there were the 2013 awards and the 2014 contract awards.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: How many of those companies are still in business, and how many of them have gone out of business?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: There were a few that opted to stop service, and so we can provide that to you, a list of the 13 vendors and the 14 vendors.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: There were a few.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: That stopped service?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: What seemed to be the issue?

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Why did they stop?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: The prevailing concern was profit.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I have some time left.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I'm going to ask about routes.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Which one of you or which office designed the routes?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So within OPT, the Office of People Transportation, we have a full routing team.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so, John, you want to talk a little about routing?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: Yes, so our team designs the routes.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: We have a team within our office called Transit Services.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: That's a team of routers that are based by borough.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: What they do is, like Kevin mentioned earlier, on August 6th, we pull all of the available student data that is in the system at that time.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: We use that data combined with school schedules that we have on file to design the bus routes.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: Those bus routes become the routes that are offered to the vendors at the PIC that Kevin mentioned as well.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: This year was on August 18th.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Is this an automated process where software does the routing or there's a manual process?

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: There's a person that assigns every student to a route.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: How does that work?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: It's a combination of the two.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: So there is some manual individual student routing, and then there's also a function within the system where you can select a group of students and it manually routes them based on where they live and the path from the residences to the school.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: So it's really a combination of the both.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: Obviously, we want to get rid of the legacy systems and replace it with the modernized via routing system, which will do it using an algorithm that is more robust and efficient and allows us to do the work more efficiently and make more efficient use of our resources.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Regarding extra routes that were added after the school starts, do you have numbers for that?

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Like how many extra routes were added after school started in September?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So after the vendor pick that you alluded to, we added, I think it was 430.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: Yes, it was about that, newly added routes from one year to the next.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And what if the current bus contractors cannot accommodate?

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: What happens to these new routes?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So most of our efforts are focused on recruitment.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so since that pick, we hired over 350 new drivers onboarded.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And each company is currently onboarding, and we get them through daily new drivers.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Can I squeeze in one more question?

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: The bus lanes that we have all over the city.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Actually, Councilor Wong, you'll ask a question in a sec.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I just want to say one thing to the DOE.

chapters.summary: Zhuang asks how DOE communicates with limited-English-proficient families; DOE describes translated materials and town halls but admits more outreach is needed.
chapters.title: Council Member Zhuang questions DOE on multilingual communication

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: The committee had previously requested data on routing information.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: The DOE had sent it.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: We had sent a clarifying question via email.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And so for any of the DOE employees in the room, we'd like the response to that question, please, before we...

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Before we continue with the next round of questions.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: But, Councilor Wong, please continue with your last question.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Bus lanes are all over the New York City.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Do the school buses use those bus lanes, or no, they cannot?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Thank you for the question.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: One of the things we did work on in years past to make sure our vendors knew that a school bus was eligible to be in a bus lane.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: But they do use it, right?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And we're thankful for that.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I have some more for round two.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Okay, great.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I will just share.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It would be worthwhile to make sure the vendors and the drivers themselves are aware that they can use the bus lanes because I can tell you they are not all aware.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So that's some of the outreach that is incumbent upon you to do.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: That's great feedback.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We'll make sure we message the vendors again tonight.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I'm going to go for second round of questions and start again with Councilmember Ressler.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I really appreciate it, Chair Dynowitz, and thank you again.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I'd like to just shift to the contracts.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: You know, the current school bus contracts in place since 1979.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Pretty remarkable and I think profoundly problematic.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Last fall, the PEP granted a three-year extension that will expire in 28.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So we should be in the process of figuring out that next procurement right now.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Could you share an update on where we are at in this process?

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I know that

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: We're concerned about the implications of the employee protection provision legislation.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Any updates you can share on that as well?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Thank you very much for the question.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: As it relates to your previous question, I want to just provide the information.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: It was so far it was $270,000 for liquidated damage for not subscribing to the route.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Do you have a time frame on that?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I can get you the window.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I think that's for September and October.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And I can get you as kind of as this looks and shakes out across the companies.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So $270K for September, October.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So on pace for a couple million dollars for the year if we don't see improved behavior.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I'd like to see improvements.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So would I.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: But, okay.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: As it relates to...

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And just to affirm, your testimony was that...

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: In every instance of a driver not turning on the GPS, a violation with a $75 fine was issued.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Do those fines escalate, and is there any increasing accountability for repeated offenders?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Well, one friendly amendment.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Each and every liquidated damage, there's an opportunity for a vendor to appeal that.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so if they said, like, the driver dropped the device in the puddle, there's a way for us to weigh in.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: So not in every single, but every one we issue the liquidated damage, and then they have an opportunity to appeal it, and there's a process for that.

chapters.summary: A Brooklyn parent testifies that their child's bus is consistently late and that the app often shows incorrect information, causing missed school time.
chapters.title: Public witness describes bus delays in Brooklyn

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So it's not $270,000 in our bank account yet as the city of New York, but those are the fines that you've issued.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And just to clarify, when there's repeat offenders, same driver doesn't turn on the GPS three days in a week, it's still $75 the third time, $75 next week, $75 the week after that?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Do we have the sliding scale in the contract provision?

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: There's no sliding scale.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: I will say repeated failures to log in are unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: What has to happen is that becomes part of the vendor report card, the subscription.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: If a company goes under a performance review in one period, it does not improve to the next.

utterances.speaker: John Benson
utterances.text: They're subject to further escalation and possible corrective action plans being put in place.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: On to the contracts.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Yeah, so I want to thank you for the, it's a very important question.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: We ultimately hear from schools, family, advocates, and many in city government about what is the future of the bus contracts.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And we know that we were given a three-year extension in the last administration, and that narrows us down to ultimately a very short window, and so time is of the...

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: Yes, and I would say in fairness, our strategy is looking at every means possible, working with our city partners, inclusive of everyone here, and so I appreciate that, and our partners in Albany as well.

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: And so when we have a little more meaningful information to share, I'll come back and share with the council, but appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Assuming we can get the EPP legislation done in the next six months.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Does that leave us enough time to issue a new procurement under the timeframe that was provided, the three-year extension?

utterances.speaker: Kevin Moran
utterances.text: I won't speculate, but there's a reason to be optimistic, so love to have that conversation if something like that happens.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: You know, at the end of the de Blasio administration, NICE bus was created.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I'm, you know, on Team Gail Brewer here.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: She and I both, you know, have been impressed by this innovative approach that you and others helped to create, much to your credit and to First Deputy Mayor Fullahan's credit.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Do you think other municipalities run their own municipal bus systems themselves?

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: We don't have these issues of shady vendors and bad technology because they're in control.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: LA runs its own bus system for 60,000 students.
