utterances.text: Another student has not had a bus route since July because a code needs to be updated on his OASIS profile and no one has updated it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Curran
utterances.text: His mother spends four hours a day transporting him to school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Curran
utterances.text: Kyle is a kindergartner with cerebral palsy who needs a para.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Curran
utterances.text: The family submitted the paperwork, the medical paperwork needed back in May, again in September.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Curran
utterances.text: No one from DOE has reviewed it, and his parents are trying to figure out ways to get him to school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Curran
utterances.text: We also represent a first grader who spent over two and a half hours on the bus on her commute home this fall, as well as students whose ridership was inexplicably deleted from OPT for no reason and lost busing for two weeks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Curran
utterances.text: Families do not have a way to address these urgent problems quickly, and many of the students I just referred to do not have busing despite repeated efforts from my office.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Curran
utterances.text: We applaud the city member, council member Ressler's bill to monitor timely bus service, which is an important step.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Curran
utterances.text: We also urge for monitoring of IEP mandated transportation accommodations, and we thank the committee for their work on this today.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Just two comments.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: One is I do want to thank the DOE.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: They still have staff members here who are taking notes.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: They are listening.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So I want to give them, you know, make sure that's highlighted.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And I would, you know, recommend after the hearing speaking to them about some of these individual cases.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Where I said it, the deputy chancellor, I know with him, you know, when we have individual cases, very often they get resolved.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Of course, we're interested in the systemic issues, but it sounds like there are, you know, efforts and steps you could take to help some of your clients.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And I do think it's, Hannah, I do think it's worth a further conversation.

chapters.summary: Wong asks about the public dashboard and data transparency; DOE says it supports Intro 835's intent and is working on a timeline.
chapters.title: Council Member Wong follows up on data dashboard and transparency

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: One of the things I spoke about earlier was, you know, how is DOE talking within itself and how is the DOE talking to like HPD about housing?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I think talking to ACS is another one of those avenues.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: making sure the transportation is aligned with an agency that's supposed to be helping kids, not adding stress to the families, you know, students with disabilities who are often already overtaxed and overstressed.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So I want to thank you for raising those issues, and I will call the next panel.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And before I call this panel, I'm going to apologize if I mispronounce any names, and you'll just correct me on the record.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Maria McGinley.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Sarah Catalinotto.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Caitlin Viatoro.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Kijindu Obiafuma.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Noelle Furbis.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I meant to say, bless you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: You sneezed earlier.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: But yeah, I was, yeah, but it was, I don't want to interrupt someone's testimony.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Bless you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And Rima Izquierda.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Go from left to my left, your right.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So we'll start with you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: State your name for the record, and you may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Dinowitz, your staff, and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: My name is Maria McGinley.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: I'm a former New York City Department of Education special education teacher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: I'm now a special education attorney and founder of the McGinley Law Group, representing New York City students with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: For these students, transportation is not simply how they get to school, it's how they access their education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: And when transportation fails, education is failing with it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: I could spend my entire two minutes recounting this year's failures alone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: A child spending five hours on a bus in one day, countless other unduly lengthy rides,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: buses that never come at all, parents risking their jobs and potentially losing their jobs to get their children to and from school, students denied mandated bus power professionals, students suspended

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: from transportation for disability-related behaviors, pre-K students who have been denied bus routes altogether,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: and perhaps most reprehensible, a child with autism who is physically

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: assaulted by the very staff entrusted with his safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: And just as Randy Levine had testified earlier, the calls to our office have not stopped.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: These aren't isolated incidents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: They reflect a system where failure is routine, accountability is elusive, and children with disabilities are paying the price.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: And the city has known about these problems for years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: Families need transparency and accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: Require public reporting of missed pickups, excessive ride times, and missing supports.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: Give families one number to call and then a firm deadline for them to get help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: Hold vendors accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: Ensure that there's appropriate training for staff who are supporting these students.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: Require the DOE to make up lost instruction and services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: Because tomorrow morning, thousands of kids are going to be at the curb waiting for the bus to come, and the city has to show up for them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria McGinley
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: My name is Caitlin Villatoro, and I'm the New York City Policy Fellow at the New York League of Conservation Voters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Genowitz and committee members for the opportunity to comment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: More than 11,000 New York City school buses transport about 150,000 students to school each day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: These buses run on diesel fuel, a major greenhouse gas emitter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: A majority of school bus depots in New York City are located in environmental justice areas, and the exhaust from these buses harms school children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Dangerous diesel exhaust exposure can lead to serious health impacts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: such as asthma, a major cause of chronic absences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: We fought for the passage of Local Law 120 of 2021, mandating an all-electric school bus fleet by 2035 to cut harmful pollutants and improve public health and air quality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Electric school buses have zero tailpipe emissions, meaning they offer clean and healthy rides as well as quieter streets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: While the city has made decent progress when it comes to being awarded electric school bus grants, not many ESBs are on the road.

chapters.summary: A Staten Island parent testifies that express bus service is limited and that students face long commutes, calling for a free express bus pilot.
chapters.title: Public witness describes bus service for students in Staten Island

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: We urge the city, specifically DOE, to fully commit to the timely implementation and funding of this law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Moreover, the city must work with school bus vendors to plan and fund school bus charging infrastructure throughout the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: We are encouraged that some bus vendors have acquired ESBs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: For instance, New York City School Bus Umbrella Services have 30 of them on the road and is working with Con Ed on EV charging.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Nice Bus is also working on a vehicle-to-grid installation, which is an energy technology that enables EVs to function as mobile batteries, discharge stored energies to the electric grid to provide a variety of benefits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: And lastly, NYLCV strongly supports the clean fuel standard at the state level.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: With CFS, high-carbon fuel providers like diesel and gasoline wholesalers must purchase credit from low-carbon fuel providers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: This bill would help lower the cost of going electric and using biofuels for diesel engine vehicles, making it cheaper for fleet operators to purchase both zero-emission vehicles and buy lower-carbon fuels.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: Moving away from fossil fuel base to electric.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: school buses is important to reduce our emissions, and we look forward to working with the council to ensure the ISB law is implemented.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: So close.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: I swear I rehearsed it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Villatoro
utterances.text: I was at 201 the whole time.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: So close.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: Good afternoon, councilmen and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: My name is Noelle Forbes, a special education attorney with also with the McGinley Law Group representing New York City students with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: Thank you for the hearing today and on how the deal we busing failures affect our clients and their families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: For our clients, transportation is not separate from their education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: If the bus does not get them to school safely and on time, they cannot receive the instruction and services they need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: In February of 2026, the parents of a student that we represent reported that their son, who has severe autism, bus routinely arrived at least 20 minutes late, costing him at least 100 minutes of instruction every week.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: The delays worsened to as much as two hours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: Sometimes the bus did not arrive at all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: His school repeatedly escalated these problems to OPT, but they continued to persist.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: Then in September, OPT assigned the student a 6-10 a.m.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: Pickup for a 9 a.m.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: School start.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: The parent asked whether his limited time travel mandate was still in place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: They explained that he had experienced escalated aggression on much shorter bus rides the previous year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: In a follow-up email, they reported that the student had already spent five hours on the bus that day and counting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: Aggression for this student looks like throwing objects and hitting peers in attendance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: By the time he reaches his school, he is completely dysregulated and unable to participate in class.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: These are not minor scheduling inconveniences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: They mean lost instruction, serious safety concerns, and a parent left asking whether their child's needs are being considered at all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: A transportation mandate on paper means nothing if the route does not honor it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: So I urge this council to demand a corrective action plan from the DOE and OPT with firm deadlines, name the officials responsible for resolving violations and public reporting on missed pickups, late arrivals, and compliance with transportation mandates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: Families need a clear escalation process that produces timely solutions, not repeated complaints without resolution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: Please, excuse me, our students should not have to lose their education minute by minute while we wait for the bus system to work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Noelle Forbes
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: That's good timing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: Perfect.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Perfect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Dinnowitz, education committee members, and my old law school classmate, Alex.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: Hi.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to speak with you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: My name is Jindio Bufuma.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: I'm the Senior Special Education Policy Manager at Advocates for Children of New York, and I'm speaking today on behalf of the ARISE Coalition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: ARISE comprises over 120 organizations, parents, educators, and advocates who have been working since 2008 to advocate for systemic solutions to the challenges faced by New York City students with disabilities and their families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: We urge the city to take affirmative steps to improve school bus service and to ensure a better busing system is in place by the time the current bus contracts expire in June 2028.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: Since the beginning of the school year, we have been made aware of countless transportation disruptions for New York City students with disabilities, including stories others have shared about students who were not given routes, students with assigned routes but no bus or driver,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: students waiting for bus pairs and unable to ride the bus without them, students waiting for the bus for over an hour or spending hours on the bus, students arriving to school late, students from multiple schools being packed onto crowded buses, and students being dropped off in the wrong locations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: When these disruptions occur, the available solutions are often neither timely nor effective.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: Parents report receiving automated responses weeks later, disjointed communication between school staff, bus company staff, and OPT.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: and a persistent lack of transparency regarding whom to contact when transportation breakdowns occur.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: Ride share alternatives, when offered, also come with additional challenges, including late arrivals and hours-long rides, which can cause undue burdens for busy parents who must schedule their days around these rides.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: Students with disabilities and their families should not have to keep waiting for the city to act.

chapters.summary: Zhuang asks about language access in bus communications; DOE says it is expanding translated materials and outreach but needs more work.
chapters.title: Council Member Zhuang follows up on language access and outreach

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: The city must improve the quality of bus service to meet students'needs by rebidding our decades-old bus contracts, addressing the shortage of drivers, attendants, paraprofessionals, and nurses,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: adding bus service for after-school and weekend programs, providing better training for school transportation coordinators, and assigning easily identifiable contacts who will take ownership for resolving transportation breakdowns in a timely manner.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: We urge the city to make these changes and make better busing a reality for all New York City students.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jindio Bufuma
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: You're allowed to breathe, by the way.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It's allowed.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: Time's on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: I'm Sarah Catalinato from Parents to Improve School Transportation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: I have way too much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: We've got emails this morning, last night.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: There are definitely real people out there with no route, no power, and those are not just numbers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: We know that the drivers can write an inspection report to get the employer to flag a problem route.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: Again, these routes come from OPT.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: And I'm raising this because we're measuring these routes that take too long, but the source of that is only partly what's happening at the base.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: They're working from what they're given.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: So if the driver says it's a problem route,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: we don't see any tracking mechanism to then say, okay, did the company then flag that to OPT as requested,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: and did OPT do something about it, and what was the timeline?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: So, for example, on the parent end, when people call and they get an incident number, and it was described about how fast and spiffy and efficient that is, blah, blah, blah,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: Actually, no, because we all know parents with dozens of incident numbers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: who don't get any response from anyone, any follow-up until and unless it's somebody like this copied or like you copied on the email.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: And that's not a system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: That's not a customer service system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: That's definitely not a pupil transportation system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: So we need a lot more thoughtfulness and we need, you know, what you're doing, which is listening to people on the ground.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: About the needs and also about any unintended consequences of this in which, let's say,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: you know, even with the, even if we get things in place to have a bid with EPP,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: There's going to be people laid off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: There's going to be talent loss.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: There's going to be some chaos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: So we need to like plans A, B, and C.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: And I love that you're talking about the workforce development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: We have some ideas and contacts for that.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I'd love to talk further about that.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I'd like to thank this panel and just reiterate something Sarah said, which is, you know,

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Often an agency sees numbers on a spreadsheet, but we see and you see people.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: These are real stories.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And each child that is not getting to school or not getting the services they deserve is not just a number on a page.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: These are people that we're supposed to be helping.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: So I want to thank this panel and thank you for reminding us of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: And I heard from Rima she's going to.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Catalinotto
utterances.text: Do that.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Our next panel is Amanda Henry McIntosh, Mike Brown.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Carolyn Richberger.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Rich.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Richberg.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I was so close.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: See you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Oh, I, well, I, I can't, it's, Muhammad Saleh and Jimmy Cortez.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Let's do right to left.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: My right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: A Manhattan parent testifies that bus routes are unreliable and that the app often fails, causing children to be late to school.
chapters.title: Public witness describes bus service for students in Manhattan

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: First and foremost, I just want to say thank you to the board and thank you, Chairman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: I've got a bit of a spiel, so I'm just going to keep this quick.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: My name is Mike.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: For the past several years, I have dedicated myself to helping improve the quality of public education for high school students throughout the New Jersey and New York district.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: I was first inducted into the public school system over COVID, where I was subbing over Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: Since then, I've garnered the privilege of teaching in person.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: Over Zoom, I had two rules, no phones and screens on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: This may seem less relevant now, but I assure you it is indefinitely relevant, as there is no greater harm to our children than the object of distraction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: But I would like to take this idea beyond the classroom, because while we can ask our students to put their phones away, keep their heads up high, and give their

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: undivided attention to their education, we must also ask ourselves, are we as a city and as a community doing everything in our power to give them the opportunity to succeed?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: It is difficult to demand punctuality from a student whose bus arrives 20 minutes late.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: It is difficult to demand consistency from a young person whose train is delayed, whose connection is unreliable, or whose commute is so expensive that simply getting to school becomes a financial burden on the family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: Chairman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: The other week, while teaching my third period, a student of mine, who I will not name the name of, loaded up a spitball into a plastic straw and shot it directly into my esophagus.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: It was a direct hit, first ricocheting off of my uvula, then lodging itself into my throat, before my body naturally rejected it, projectile vomiting onto the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: the floor leaving schmutz all over me and embarrassment inside of me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: I know this is not the most pleasant thing to hear, believe me, but I must ask the council this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: Why am I the one who shall be punished for this offense?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: I understand my appearance is odder than usual, but what have I done to deserve this?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: My life is ruined from this permanently.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: So now I am here not only demanding justice from the council, but encouraging parents to look deeper into their child's behaviors and the systemic issues that cause these behaviors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: What are our kids being told?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: What are they looking at?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Brown
utterances.text: And what are they sharing while they're waiting for these buses?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you, Chairman.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: May we begin?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Dinowitz and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: My name is Jimmy Cortez and I'm from Woodhaven.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: It's a pleasure to speak before you today on this matter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: It's been a recurring issue for years and we're finally seeing concrete action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: Scorecards have been released to the public and while good, I have some suggestions for improvements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: The data missing

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: is their on-time performance, and this was already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: And we thank Council Member Ressler and Chair Dinowitz for introducing legislation that would fix this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: Companies on the reports, in my opinion, should be divided into sections that establish a main public grade that should be easily understood by the public.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: We may use existing terms such as exceeding expectations, meeting them, and needing improvement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: It should focus primarily on performance and safety so that the public may know how well their provider companies perform.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: The release date of these can be included in school calendars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: Any other data is important and should be used by the department for prevention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: An incident was mentioned by a council member earlier about a bus going off course with disabled children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: her child.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: Incidents like these cause a lack of trust in the system and would be easily prevented if consequences were enforced, such as penalties and having the underperforming companies exposed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: Bus companies cannot keep self-reporting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: I equate that to asking a toddler if he ate all the chocolate while he has residue on his mouth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: This ties into what was found on the comptroller's audit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: The department has been reactive, relying on outside sources rather than their own findings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: Oversight of operations must be taken seriously to ensure the safety and fulfillment of the educational requirements of young New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jimmy Cortez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: You already know my name, and the chairperson messed it up, but it's okay.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Would you say it anyway for the record?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Richburg.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa asks about the procurement process for new bus contracts; DOE says it is preparing a solicitation and will prioritize accountability.
chapters.title: Council Member De La Rosa follows up on contract procurement

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Richburg, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: You said Richburger.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Well, you know, it kind of like trails off at the end with the picture.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Yeah, you know, I'm going to pick on you because you said in the beginning, kids don't read books.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: They, you know, and I thought that was important because kids are not reading books.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: But, you know, when you, it's not so much about mispronouncing names, but you got to have the skill to know how to break down the words so that you can say them correctly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: But that's another story.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Anyway.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: You're a slip for the record so anyone else can see the handwriting on this, to be fair.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: But please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Is my handwriting?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I regret to inform you, yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: We're going to check that one out.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Let's do it.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Let's do it together.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: I don't mean any harm, but long time Bethesda-Iverson resident, been in the school system over 50 years, started as a young teacher, know all about everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: But transportation, I never really paid attention to, and I hope my time don't exceed itself.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: We'll give you the 20 seconds extra, don't worry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Okay, but you know, like, if you're going to reduce variation, let's say,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: How can you reduce variation?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: I'm talking about transportation and all the problems with transportation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: I don't want to keep repeating things because we're all getting tired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: But the thing of it is, how are you going to reduce a problem and try to hit the target if you keep...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: repeating the problem like insanity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: You know the contracts are no good.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: You have to update the contracts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: You know that different levels of people in the city are getting, receiving different things because of, I don't want to say discrimination, but for whatever reason.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: You come out with disability, but there's a whole lot of

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: discriminatory practices that people are putting against people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: But what I'm saying is, if the bus system is really bad, you have to really work on that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: And the way you work on things is that you have to cut people's money off when they don't comply.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: So, you know, we can say this and we can say that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: But my conclusion, you should cut those contracts out or get something that you can live with and the city can live with.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: But you shouldn't keep giving contracts to people who are not maintaining

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: and hitting the target by getting children to school on time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Because we know the results of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: So we're not going to keep going over that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: What we have to do is look at them contracts you're giving out to what companies, and they have to respect us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: That's what I want to say, and I thank you for my time.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You've got a couple more seconds if you want to say anything else.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: No, I'm just glad to be here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: And I'm going to start coming to all the meetings.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We're glad to have you here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Yes, I'm going to start coming to all the meetings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: It's important.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: They're fun.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Yeah, they are.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richburg
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Genovitz and member of the Education Committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: Thank you for inviting me to speak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: My name is Mohamed Salim.

chapters.summary: A Brooklyn parent testifies that bus service has worsened this year, with frequent cancellations and lack of communication, and asks for immediate relief.
chapters.title: Public witness describes bus service for students in Brooklyn

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: I serve as Vice President of Citywide Council on High School.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: representing Staten Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: I'm a proud Pakistani immigrant and father of four.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: My daughter graduated as valedictorian of Staten Island Technical High School in 2025.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: One day she came home and told me her teachers believed someone in her class could one day win a Nobel Prize.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: That reminded me what makes America special.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: We encourage our children to dream big, but we must also help them get there.

chapters.summary: He describes long commutes and costs for Staten Island students, asks the committee to work with DOE and MTA on a free express bus pilot, and suggests student-only fares or federal grants.
chapters.title: Mohamed Salim calls for free express bus pilot for Staten Island students

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: On September 16, our council passed a resolution calling for free express bus access for eligible public high school students.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: For Staten Island students, long commutes, multiple transfers, and transportation costs can limit educational opportunities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: Express buses are not a luxury for these students.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: They can be a necessity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: Today I ask this committee to work with New York City Public Schools and MTA to launch a free express bus pilot program on Staten Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: The pilot could measure commute times, attendance, punctuality, and family transport cost.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: If full funding is not immediately possible, student only could cover the regular fare with families paying the difference.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: We should also explore

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: federal educational and transportation grants to help fund this initiative.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: Our children could choose school based on their dreams and abilities, not the difficulty of getting there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: I've spoken to various city councilmen and have got support from

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: Frank Mariano, I spoke with Senator Lou last night as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: He's in support of this as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mohamed Salim
utterances.text: You're welcome.

chapters.summary: Mother of five, four autistic, recounts July 20 incident where nonverbal son Nyesi was dropped at the wrong school, no one reported it, and DOE investigation still lacks findings; calls for trained staff, verified handoffs, and enforceable safety contracts.
chapters.title: Amanda McIntosh describes nonverbal son dropped at wrong school

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Member Denowitz and other members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: My name is Amanda McIntosh.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: I'm a mother of five boys, four of whom are autistic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: Every morning I entrust school transportation with something far more precious than a route number, my children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: Last year I removed my son's bus pass so that he could attend school consistently and on time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: On July 20th, my nonverbal son, Nyesi, boarded his bus at 7.20 a.m.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: And at 8.21, I learned he had been dropped off at the wrong school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: Another child arrived at his school in his place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: Neither school had contact information for the driver or matron.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: They called me to get those numbers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: Had they not needed those numbers, I wonder what they have told me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: Nearly four months later, neither the driver, the matron, nor either school has independently reported this incident.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: Mine was the only report on record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: I have to add that I had to request an apology because unfortunately that was not an instinct.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: Naissi cannot say, I don't belong here or I'm in the wrong place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: His lack of a voice that holds volume does not remove his experience of fear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: Yesterday, DOE Incident Response Director Christina Pagan called me for the second time, still without any findings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: I had to insist on a reference number after being told the investigation had been outsourced to SCI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: I did get a cheerful happy holidays, though.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: The deal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: East Director of Transportation asked that we resolve this

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: issue behind closed doors?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: If OPT has clear safety protocols and an incident response team, how did this happen?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: OPT's immediate response was a priority ticket.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: No response or follow-up and an automated closure of that ticket and consistent I don't know answers from staff across the board.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: This is a public safety issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: We need trained staff, verified handoffs, immediate parent notification, mandatory incident reporting, and enforceable safety contracts with true consequences when violated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: That incident still echoes in Naisee's behavior.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: The damage isn't measured in dollars or minutes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: It's measured in memories that cannot be undone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: Mothers left fearful and nonverbal children left in hallways and schoolyards where they don't belong.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Henry McIntosh
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: He acknowledges her hard job and love for her children, and thanks her for fighting.
chapters.title: Dinowitz thanks McIntosh for sharing difficult story

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you for sharing that story.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: You have absolutely the hardest job in the world, and it's so clear how much you love your children, how you're not going to stop fighting for them, and we so appreciate you in our city.

chapters.summary: He thanks Ms. Richburg for visiting, says bus companies have held the city over a barrel, threaten strikes when the city tries to remove bad contractors, and same vendors have had contracts since 1979.
chapters.title: Restler criticizes bus companies holding city hostage

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Councilmember Ressler has a question for the panel.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Just wanted to say that it's good to see you, Ms.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Richburg.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thank you for coming in to visit us at the council.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I couldn't agree with your sentiments more.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: You know, these school bus companies have held the city over a barrel forever.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And whenever the city's tried to say, let's get rid of bad contractors, let's get rid of these folks that are not delivering, they threaten to go on strike.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And that, and then it puts our kids at risk.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And so the city has...

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: succumb to that pressure too many times.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler

chapters.summary: Parent of kindergarten twins with IEPs says they have had no appropriate route since school began, estimated 2-3 hour travel, 6:30 a.m. pickup for 8:15 school, and five-year-olds placed on buses with high schoolers; asks for timely IEP accommodations and developmentally appropriate routes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: As a parent of two kindergarten students with IEPs, I'm here to address the ongoing transportation failures that have affected my family since the beginning of the school year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: My twins have been without an appropriate bus route since school began.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: Initially, we were given estimated travel time of two to three hours, requiring my children to be downstairs as early as 6.30 a.m., potentially earlier with preparation beginning around 5.30 a.m.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: The bus company could not consistently provide accurate pickup times because

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: Routes depended on daily attendance and available space.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: This was despite our children's school being approximately 30 minutes away and not opening until 8.15.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: Even after their IEPs reflected a travel time limitation of less than 30 minutes,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: The DOE has still failed to provide an appropriate route.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: Equally concerning is the placement of five-year-old kindergartners on buses filled with high school students.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: Our own bus drivers and matrons have expressed concerns about the potential safety and appropriateness of these arrangements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: My children already have sensory sensitivities and require additional support with regulation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: Their transportation environment should not introduce unnecessary distress or compromise their safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: I believe transportation for students with disabilities must consider the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: Elemental differences where appropriate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: Younger students in grades K to 5 should be grouped together, grades 6 to 8 together, and grades 9 to 12 together.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: I am asking NYC to prioritize timely implementation of IEP transportation accommodations, enforce individualized

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: travel time limits, establish developmentally appropriate routes, and hold the DOE accountable when these services are not provided.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: Transportation is not a privilege or an optional convenience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: It is an essential part of a child's access to education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: Our children deserve to arrive to school safely, regulated, and ready to learn.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony, but your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Espino
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Selena Haygood

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Selena Haygood

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Selena Haygood

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Selena Haygood

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Selena Haygood

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Selena Haygood

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Single parent of five-year-old with multiple disabilities says son's IEP requires limited travel time and climate control, but not met; she has many tickets and gets ping-ponged between DOE and OPT; child misses services and has regression in potty training.
chapters.title: Elizabeth Hammond says son's IEP travel and climate mandates violated

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Elizabeth Hammond.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: I'm a single parent of a beautiful five-year-old child with multiple disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: My son has limited time travel, climate control mandates indicated in his IEP, which are not being met.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: His faith is being violated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: His civil rights are being violated and nothing is being done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: I have so many tickets in and still all the parents get is ping pong from DOE to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: To back to OPT and there's no resolve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: They need to do better.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: This is the most vulnerable population.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: Parents trust OPT to do better and they need to do better.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: There's so many issues that I can talk about from being late every day to school to hour and a half long rides, regression and potty training.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: My child misses services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: He can't come out of the pull up because he's on the bus for extended periods of time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: It's just so horrible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: And parents need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: We need resolve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: We need to know who we can contact and we really do need help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Hammond
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: He thanks her, calls Swati Kim, then Thomas Fret when Kim does not respond.
chapters.title: Dinowitz thanks Hammond and calls next remote witnesses

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Next we have Swati Kim.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Okay, we're Thomas Fret.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thomas Fret.

chapters.summary: He says he cannot testify but submitted written testimony, urges everyone to read it, and looks forward to working with city council, mayor, and parents to solve the bus crisis.
chapters.title: Thomas Fret submits written testimony and calls for collaboration

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Fret
utterances.text: Hi, good evening.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Fret
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: We can, yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Fret
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Fret
utterances.text: Good evening, Councilmember Dino Witz and the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Fret
utterances.text: Thank you for having me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Fret
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I will not be able to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Fret
utterances.text: I did submit a written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Fret
utterances.text: Please read it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Fret
utterances.text: I urge everyone to read it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Fret
utterances.text: I look forward to working with the city council, with the mayor and his team and parents to solve this school bus crisis.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: We'll look at that written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And then we have Camila Newton.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Recent law grad and parent says on Nov 12 her daughter's AM and PM routes were disrupted despite IEP door-to-door entitlement; tracker showed route inactive; OPT said DOE re-evaluated and deemed her ineligible; no advance notification or written explanation; grandmother had to change schedule.
chapters.title: Camila Newton describes daughter's bus route abruptly canceled

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: Hi, good evening.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: I don't know if it's too loud here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: Can everyone hear me, King?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: You're fine, yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: Okay, good.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: My name is Camila, and although I'm a recent law grad, I'm actually here on behalf of my long-distance clients, my C-Mess babies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: On Thursday, November 12th, my daughter's school bus route, both of her routes, her AM and PM routes, were abruptly disrupted despite her entitlement to door-to-door transportation under her IEP.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: I was out of town when this happened, and my grandmother was downstairs waiting for the bus, and she had been on time every morning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: When it didn't arrive, I checked the tracker and discovered the route was no longer active.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: I immediately contacted the person they were with, which hopefully proves to be a challenge in many respects, but I've learned some facts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: To get someone to answer the phone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: They said that the issue must have been an OPT mistake, a phone OPT, and OPT reps that I spoke to actually argued down that there was no mistake made and read to me a spiel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: that explained that the Department of Education had been doing re-evaluations of children who they believed were too close to the school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: And that my daughter was somehow deemed ineligible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: When I requested documentation of that conversation, the service ticket was closed without any meaningful documentation of the conversation that was held and put the onus on the school to then fix the issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: When I spoke to the school principal, she acknowledged that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: She had been having these conversations with the Department of Education and did not expect them to, did not expect the changes to be implemented in this way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: Parents received no advance notification.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: And today I've received no written explanation about what occurred.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: To that end, I mean, even if the explanation was that she lived too close to the school, her PM route does not take her home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: It takes her to after school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: And so she has not been in after school for the last week now, and some change.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: And, you know, my grandmother has had to disrupt her own schedule in order to be there to pick her up from school because now there's no bus.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Newton
utterances.text: Okay, thank you all.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

chapters.summary: He asks if anyone else present wants to testify, thanks DOE and all who testified, calls it a crisis, and adjourns.
chapters.title: Dinowitz thanks testifiers and adjourns hearing

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: If there is anyone else present in the room who has not had the opportunity to testify but wishes to do so, please raise your hand.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I'd like to thank the Department of Education, everyone who testified today, everyone who sent testimony to us about what I would call a crisis in our school system.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Kids not getting to school or in untenable situations if they do have busing.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And this is something we're going to continue to push on because it's no less than our children deserve.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And with that, this hearing is adjourned.

summary: Committee on Education held an oversight hearing on NYC school bus transportation, focusing on delays, missed pickups, and accountability for contractors.
DOE Deputy Chancellor Kevin Moran testified about the scale of the system, app usage, vendor report cards, and challenges from a 31% growth in curb-to-school transportation demand.
Council members, parents, and advocates described widespread failures, including long rides, missed routes, safety incidents, and called for stronger oversight, penalties, and new contracts.
title: Committee on Education
topic: Oversight - Examining School Bus Transportation Services in NYC
